title: Inside the store, 1986 to 2018
lede: A reference history says FAO Schwarz “did not advertise” in the years that made it famous, and we found few commercials to show.[^9] What survives is footage of the store itself: visitors’ tapes and news reports of the closing and the return. Where a date comes only from the uploader, the caption says so.

videos.title: “Browsing toys and video games at FAO Schwarz in 1986”
videos.caption: Twelve minutes of amateur video inside the store, uploaded by the channel Vampire Robot. The 1986 date is the uploader’s; if it is right, this is the year the flagship moved to 767 Fifth Avenue.[^9][^33]

videos.title: “FAO Schwarz Toy Store 1995”
videos.caption: Seven minutes of footage uploaded by the archive channel tvdays, which dates it 1995. We could not confirm the date or the original broadcaster.[^34]

videos.title: Associated Press: “Game Over: FAO Schwarz Toy Store Closes”
videos.caption: The AP’s report on the closing of the Fifth Avenue flagship in July 2015, from its own channel.[^22]

videos.title: AP Archive: “Beloved toy store FAO Schwarz makes its NYC return”
videos.caption: AP footage of the new store at 30 Rockefeller Plaza, which opened on November 16, 2018.[^29]

videos.title: TODAY: “FAO Schwarz Reopens: Peek Inside The Iconic Toy Store”
videos.caption: NBC’s morning show visits the new store. NBC is a neighbor: the store took over the space of the NBC Experience Store.[^28]

note: We found no embeddable footage of the 2003 bankruptcies or of the 1986 opening that we could date with confidence.
